system_overview: This specification models a high-level voting-based consensus algorithm in which a set of acceptor processes cooperatively choose a single value. It is a high-level abstraction of the Paxos consensus algorithm that abstracts away the details of message passing. The algorithm ensures that once a value is chosen (by receiving votes from a quorum of acceptors in the same ballot), no different value can ever be chosen.
actors_and_components: The system has three types of participants: (1) Acceptors -- processes that cast votes for values in numbered ballots. (2) Quorums -- sets of acceptors, where any two quorums must share at least one acceptor. (3) Values -- the set of values that can be proposed and chosen. There are no explicit proposer or leader roles; the algorithm focuses on how acceptors cast votes.
state_variables: The system tracks two pieces of state per acceptor: (1) the set of votes that each acceptor has cast, where each vote is a pair of a ballot number and a value; and (2) a promise threshold for each acceptor, indicating the minimum ballot number in which the acceptor will participate going forward (initialized to negative one, meaning no promise has been made).
initial_state: Initially, no acceptor has cast any votes (each acceptor's vote set is empty) and no acceptor has made any promise (each acceptor's threshold is negative one).
actions: There are two types of transitions: (1) An acceptor may increase its promise threshold to any higher ballot number without casting a vote. This prevents the acceptor from voting in any ballot below the new threshold. (2) An acceptor may vote for a value in a ballot, subject to four conditions: the ballot number must not be below the acceptor's current threshold; the acceptor must not have already voted in that ballot; no other acceptor may have voted for a different value in that same ballot; and there must exist a quorum demonstrating that the value is safe at that ballot number. Casting a vote also updates the acceptor's threshold to the ballot number. A value is safe at ballot number b if, for every lower ballot c, there exists a quorum in which every member has either voted for that value in ballot c or can never vote in ballot c.
safety_properties: Consistency: the set of chosen values contains at most one value. That is, if a quorum of acceptors have all voted for the same value in some ballot, and a quorum have all voted for some value in another ballot, those values must be the same. This follows from three invariants: (a) every vote cast is safe at its ballot number, (b) at most one value is voted for per ballot across all acceptors, and (c) the type correctness of votes and thresholds.
model_bounds: The set of ballot numbers is the natural numbers. For model checking, ballot numbers are bounded to a finite range (for example, zero through one or zero through two). The sets of acceptors, values, and quorums are declared as constants and instantiated with small finite sets for model checking.
additional_assumptions: The specification assumes that quorums satisfy the overlap property: any two quorums have a non-empty intersection. This is essential for the consistency guarantee. Ballot numbers are natural numbers. The specification includes a proof outline showing that the invariant is preserved, and it instantiates the abstract consensus specification to prove that the voting algorithm implements consensus via a refinement mapping where the chosen set is derived from the votes. The specification includes formal proofs checked by a proof system backend.
